stories.headline: MITCHELL REGRETS CAMPUS GUNFIRE
stories.summary: Atty Gen Mitchell, in referring to shootings, says Amer educ is experiencing its saddest semester in its history, s to Miss Delta business leaders, Delta State Coll; bars comment on matters now under investigation but says nation is determined to live within law and that neither violent demonstrations nor unrestrained reactions are part of law

stories.headline: NIXON WILL BAR HOSTILE COMMENTS ON STUDENTS BYA GNEW AND OTHERS; SUMMONS 50 GOVERNORS TO MEETING
stories.summary: group of prominent Harvard profs, including E O Reischauer, A Yarmolinsky and R E Neustadt, will conf with Nixon aide Dr Kissinger and publicly announce their break with Adm policies on SE Asia; disclosures reveal that Repubs had set up special telephone system to encourage calls to White House backing Nixon's policy; White House denies it

stories.headline: U.S. Will Give Cambodia $7.5.Million in Weapons
stories.summary: Adm informs Sen Foreign Relations Com it has decided to give about $7.5-million worth of arms to Cambodia on ground that such aid is important to US security, lr to Fulbright accompanied by document signed by Nixon on importance to US security; lr is classified as secret; Fulbright seeks to have classification changed that issue might be openly discussed

stories.headline: With Little Fanfare, Mexican Supreme Court Legalizes Same-Sex Marriage
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of Mexico has said laws on the books in most of the country’s states are discriminatory, but gay couples still need costly injunctions from lower courts in order to wed.

stories.headline: The Story of New York’s First Black Police Officer, Told With the Help of Langston Hughes
stories.summary: The story of Samuel J. Battle, the first black officer in the New York Police Department, is being told in a new book by Arthur Browne, a veteran newspaper reporter and editor.

stories.headline: Bizarre Court Case Puts a Violinist, and Leipzig String Quartet, in an Unflattering Light
stories.summary: Stefan Arzberger, a member of the music group, is fighting charges that he attacked a woman in a Manhattan hotel this spring.

stories.headline: For Swapped Taliban Prisoners From Guantánamo Bay, Few Doors to Exit Qatar
stories.summary: As the United States pressed Qatar for a six-month travel ban for the former Guantánamo detainees exchanged for Sgt. Bowe Bergdahl, no countries appeared eager to let them in.
